elec-resistor-physical.observed_visual_construction: The left component has a cylindrical body, multiple annular bands, rounded ends and one straight coaxial lead at each end.
elec-resistor-physical.intended_adaptation: Side elevation: cylindrical outline with two leads, simple end boundaries and a restrained set of uncolored band outlines.
elec-resistor-physical.limits: Reference is a specific marked thin-film example; the icon does not assign a color code, resistance, tolerance or dimensions.

elec-resistor-schematic.observed_visual_construction: The Resistor row uses an empty horizontal rectangle connected to a line at the midpoint of each short side.
elec-resistor-schematic.intended_adaptation: Keep the existing rectangular two-terminal resistor, with plain connection stubs.
elec-resistor-schematic.limits: This is a selected circuit-drawing convention, not evidence of formal IEC compliance.

elec-capacitor-physical.observed_visual_construction: Nichicon shows a sleeved radial can with two parallel leads and the positive lead longer; KEMET labels the contrasting lengthwise sleeve stripe negative and illustrates unequal leads.
elec-capacitor-physical.intended_adaptation: Keep the polarized radial side view, with negative marks on the left sleeve stripe, a shorter left lead and a longer right lead.
elec-capacitor-physical.limits: Example is polarized and distinct from the separate unpolarized schematic; no part size, rating or wiring instruction is assigned.
elec-capacitor-physical.access_status: both sources opened and visually inspected

elec-capacitor-schematic.observed_visual_construction: Ohio Figure 3 uses two equal straight parallel plates separated by a gap, with one centered lead on each outside face. DOE also shows this fixed-capacitor alternative.
elec-capacitor-schematic.intended_adaptation: Keep equal plates with centered straight stubs and no polarity mark.
elec-capacitor-schematic.limits: This separate unpolarized notation should not be paired as a wiring representation of the illustrated electrolytic package.

elec-inductor-physical.observed_visual_construction: Vishay shows a cylindrical axial-leaded bobbin product with one straight lead at each end; its photo has a protective sleeve. MIT shows a bare helix around a dark cylindrical core with leads bent in the same direction.
elec-inductor-physical.intended_adaptation: Synthesize an illustrative exposed winding in a side view, with a core/bobbin and axial leads to preserve the existing model meaning.
elec-inductor-physical.limits: No one figure establishes this exact combination: the Vishay product is sleeved and the MIT example has radial leads. It is an explanatory composite, not a specific manufacturer part.

elec-inductor-schematic.observed_visual_construction: Ohio shows a connected sequence of four semicircular humps in a line without a core mark; DOE Figure 1 shows an uncored winding as an alternative representation.
elec-inductor-schematic.intended_adaptation: Use a clear four-arc coil with straight end stubs and no parallel core lines.
elec-inductor-schematic.limits: Coil orientation and number of drawn arcs are presentation choices; no magnetic core material is specified.

elec-diode-physical.observed_visual_construction: A short cylindrical axial glass body has one lead on each side and a single shaded band at one end labeled cathode identification.
elec-diode-physical.intended_adaptation: Side elevation with narrow end band, cylindrical outline and coaxial leads; position the band at the right.
elec-diode-physical.limits: The right-side band follows the source marking concept but is illustrative, not a wiring instruction or exact DO-41 dimension.

elec-diode-schematic.observed_visual_construction: The Illinois slide shows an unfilled triangle pointing right into a perpendicular vertical bar with straight left/right leads; DOE shows the filled-triangle variant.
elec-diode-schematic.intended_adaptation: Use the source-observed unfilled variant with anode lead left and cathode bar right.
elec-diode-schematic.limits: Source conventions differ in fill; this diagram adopts the Illinois outline and makes no formal-standard compliance claim.

elec-transistor-physical.observed_visual_construction: The front view has a shallow rectangular molded body above three separate parallel leads; vertical lines near the body edges indicate end bevels, while the bottom view shows the chamfered outline.
elec-transistor-physical.intended_adaptation: Use a coherent front view of a TO-92-like three-lead package with end bevel boundaries and straight parallel leads.
elec-transistor-physical.limits: The example is a package outline; no pinout, type or actual dimensions are assigned.

elec-transistor-schematic.observed_visual_construction: DOE Figure 2 shows a left base bar, collector branch upper right and emitter branch lower right with arrow pointing outward; the source encloses the mark in a circle.
elec-transistor-schematic.intended_adaptation: Preserve the original uncircled NPN mark, left base and outward lower-right emitter arrow, on straight connection stubs.
elec-transistor-schematic.limits: The enclosing circle is omitted as an allowed local simplification; no pin numbering or package is implied.

elec-integrated-circuit-physical.observed_visual_construction: Top-view package figure has an elongated rectangle with an indentation centered in one short edge and four lead positions on each long side.
elec-integrated-circuit-physical.intended_adaptation: Top view of a notched eight-position dual-inline package with four individually outlined pins on each side.
elec-integrated-circuit-physical.limits: The source shows a particular eight-pin receiver; icon assigns neither its pin functions nor dimensions.

elec-integrated-circuit-schematic.observed_visual_construction: A rectangular IC block has line connections on the left and right, with pin numbers and named functions shown in the actual circuit.
elec-integrated-circuit-schematic.intended_adaptation: Generalize to the existing blank four-terminal rectangle with two line connections on each side; omit specific pin identifiers and functions.
elec-integrated-circuit-schematic.limits: The cited device has fourteen labeled pins; a generic four-terminal block is a local abstraction and does not describe that product or an actual pinout.

elec-transformer-physical.observed_visual_construction: The DOE core-type teaching figure shows one closed rectangular iron core, with two separate helical windings wound around opposite vertical limbs and each winding ending in a separate circuit. The indicated flux lines and external test circuits are explanatory, not physical components.
elec-transformer-physical.intended_adaptation: Independently redraw a compact front construction with a closed core and two distinct winding groups around its limbs; omit external circuit, flux lines, labels, dimensions and ratings.
elec-transformer-physical.limits: A simplified teaching construction, not a specific manufacturer part or a claim about leakage, turns ratio, lamination, dimensions or field strength.
elec-transformer-physical.access_status: opened and visually inspected before revision

elec-transformer-schematic.observed_visual_construction: DOE Figure 1 shows two separate opposing coil marks, four conductor ends and parallel lines between the coils for a magnetic-core transformer.
elec-transformer-schematic.intended_adaptation: Retain an independently constructed pair of opposing coil marks separated by two core lines, four plain connection stubs and no polarity dots.
elec-transformer-schematic.limits: A schematic convention; no material, ratio, rating or formal-standard compliance is asserted.
elec-transformer-schematic.access_status: opened and visually inspected before revision
